newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products weaker, freight still a concern.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products weaker, freight still a concern.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to softer on Friday.

Gasoline was $1 or so weaker to $217 cif Med, pressured by weaker NYMEX and easier crude. High freight rates in the region was also hampering activity. A requirement for 10-20,000 tonnes of material was seen into Lebanon.
Naphtha was also easier by $1 at $219 cif Med and trade quietened by freight concerns. "Traders don't want to buy and get caught with high freight costs," said one dealer.
But there was a glimmer of hope. Shipbrokers said 27,500 tonnes of naphtha was attracting W300 against W330 last week.
Gas oil sank back into inactivity because of high shipping rates after managing subdued trade on Thursday.

Russian 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was around unchanged. A cargo of Russian was bid at cif high quotes -$0.75 basis Genoa and offered at around cif high +$0.50 basis Genoa. Shipping remains prohibitively expensive at Worldscale rates 250-300 for cross-Mediterranean voyages.

The Indian Oil Corp awarded 14 cargoes of high speed diesel totalling 580,000 tonnes for March delivery, but most of it was due to come from the Middle East Gulf, adding bearish pressure to diesel in the Med.
High sulphur fuel oil was steady to softer in the Med. Dealers said they saw little activity. A tender for 20,000 tonnes of fuel oil for Dakar was heard won by a French refiner.

Straight-run fuel oil was not in good supply. A trader holding an F-5 cargo out of Sevastopol, with viscosity below two Engler, was offering at $10 a tonne over the mean/mean/mean of published quotes. Low sulphur fuel oil was quieter. Best offers into Italy were heard at $118 cif. These follow two deals on Thursday in NWE. But the market remains long, and dealers feel there is little room for upwards movement.
